In [[algebraic topology]], a '''complex-orientable cohomology theory''' is a [[multiplicative cohomology theory]] ''E'' such that the restriction map <math>E^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty) \to E^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^1)</math> is surjective. An element of <math>E^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty)</math> that restricts to the canonical generator of the reduced theory <math>\widetilde{E}^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^1)</math> is called a '''complex orientation'''. The notion is central to [[Daniel Quillen|Quillen]]'s work relating cohomology to [[formal group law]]s.{{citation needed|date=October 2013}}<!-- a bit vague -->

If <math>E</math> is an even-graded theory meaning <math>\pi_3 E = \pi_5 E = \cdots=0</math>, then <math>E</math> is complex-orientable. This follows from the [[Atiyah–Hirzebruch spectral sequence]]. 

Examples:
*An ordinary cohomology with any coefficient ring ''R'' is complex orientable, as <math>\operatorname{H}^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty; R) \simeq \operatorname{H}^2(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^1;R)</math>.
*Complex ''K''-theory, denoted ''KU'', is complex-orientable, as it is even-graded. ([[Bott periodicity theorem]])
*[[Complex cobordism]], whose spectrum is denoted by MU, is complex-orientable.

A complex orientation, call it ''t'', gives rise to a formal group law as follows: let ''m'' be the multiplication
:<math>\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty \times \mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty \to \mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty, ([x], [y]) \mapsto [xy]</math>
where <math>[x]</math> denotes a line passing through ''x'' in the underlying vector space <math>\mathbb{C}[t]</math> of <math>\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty</math>.  This is the map classifying the tensor product of the universal line bundle over <math> \mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty </math>. Viewing
:<math>E^*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty) = \varprojlim E^*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^n) = \varprojlim R[t]/(t^{n+1}) = R[\![t]\!], \quad R =\pi_* E </math>,
let <math>f = m^*(t)</math> be the pullback of ''t'' along ''m''. It lives in
:<math>E^*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty \times \mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^\infty) = \varprojlim E^*(\mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^n \times \mathbb{C}\mathbf{P}^m) = \varprojlim R[x,y]/(x^{n+1},y^{m+1}) = R[\![x, y]\!]</math>
and one can show, using properties of the tensor product of line bundles, it is a formal group law (e.g., satisfies associativity).
